targets.summary: The change makes the earlier lint_found logic (around line 385) confusing or redundant: lint_found now seems to always be True, so the command would always exit with sys.exit(1). The control flow needs clarifying or fixing.
targets.adoption_evidence: The comment sits on a blank line (412, just after `spin.util.run(cmd)`), but it is about the `lint_found` logic in `_run_lintrunner`/`lint`. That logic had been inverted: `lint_found = not bool(p.returncode)` made lint_found True on success, and the early `if not lint_found_all: ... raise SystemExit(1)` meant the command effectively always exited with status 1. The merged code fixes this. It changes the assignment to `lint_found = bool(p.returncode)`, deletes the confusing early-exit block (`if not lint_found_all: if write_json_output: ... raise SystemExit(1)`), and sets `lint_found = False` when no linters are left after the --take/--skip filters. Now the final `if lint_found: click.secho("Lint failed!", fg="red"); raise SystemExit(1)` runs only when lintrunner returns non-zero. That answers the maintainer's question: lint_found is no longer always True and the exit is no longer unconditional.
targets.stage3_reason: The comment is phrased as a question, but it points at a real inverted-logic bug: `lint_found = not bool(p.returncode)` is True when lintrunner succeeds, so the `if not lint_found_all: raise SystemExit(1)` and the final `if lint_found` checks fire backwards. The merged code changed it to `lint_found = bool(p.returncode)` and removed the inverted early exit, and a reviewer reading the code could spot the inversion.
